..Title
Chief Administrative Office recommending the Board:
1) Receive and file the FY 2026-27 Bridge Funding and Sustainability Plan prepared and submitted by National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) El Dorado County Western Slope and South Lake Tahoe, as directed by the Board on September 22, 2026, and direct staff to work with NAMI to provide an update to the Board on implementation of the Plan in the first quarter of 2027;
2) Find that a public benefit is derived from supporting NAMI's Clubhouse Program;
3) Approve and authorize the Chair to sign Funding Out Agreement 10670 with NAMI in the amount of $300,000 for the retroactive performance period of October 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, to support their Clubhouse Program; and
4) Authorize the Purchasing Agent to execute amendments relating to Agreement 10670, contingent upon approval by County Counsel and Risk Management, which do not increase the maximum dollar amount or term of the Agreement.

FUNDING: General Fund.
..Body
DISCUSSION / BACKGROUND
On September 22, 2026, with Legistar file 26-1515, the Board directed a change to the proposed FY 2026-27 Adopted Budget to “obligate up to $300,000 from General Fund Contingency for Clubhouse El Dorado and work with Clubhouse El Dorado to develop a plan and on an as needed basis to fund them through June 30, 2027, with the understanding that the County will not be opting into BH Connect and direct staff to return to the Board with an update before the end of the calendar year.”

NAMI has prepared a FY 2026-27 Bridge Funding and Sustainability Plan; attached to this item as Attachment A. The Plan outlines that Clubhouse El Dorado requires approximately $530,000 to $600,000 annually to sustain current operations. NAMI’s sustainable funding plan outlines a diversified revenue model combining healthcare
reimbursement and partnerships, public funding, foundation grants, individual philanthropy, corporate support, community fundraising, and other contracted revenue opportunities. The Plan includes NAMI providing a Mid-Year Progress Report by March 1, 2027. The Plan also includes a FY 2026-27 Budget for the Clubhouse Program.

Agreement 10670 is being presented for Board approval. This Funding Out Agreement will allow for three quarterly payments of $100,000 to NAMI for the period of October 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. A one-month retroactive performance period is recommended to allow for a full three quarters of funding and to allow the largest period of bridge funding in alignment with the Board’s direction on September 22, 2026. Prior to the payment of the second and third quarter payments, NAMI will submit a request for payment that includes an update on the implementation of the funding sustainability plan and a statement of the ongoing need for the funding. 

ALTERNATIVES
The Board could choose not to approve the proposed Agreement and could provide alternate direction.

PRIOR BOARD ACTION
See above.

OTHER DEPARTMENT / AGENCY INVOLVEMENT
County Counsel and Risk Management have reviewed the Agreement. 

FINANCIAL IMPACT
Agreement 10670 was funded through a reduction of General Fund Contingency, per Board direction provided on September 22, 2026, with Legistar file 26-1515. Appropriations for the Agreement were included in the Board-approved budget for General Revenues and Non-Departmental Expenses, also known as Department 15.

CLERK OF THE BOARD FOLLOW UP ACTIONS
If approved, obtain the Chair’s signature on Agreement 10670.

2) Approve and authorize the HHSA Director or Chief Assistant Director to execute seven funding-out agreements with various organizations supporting veterans, and to distribute the FY 2026-27 funds in the total amount of $175,000, as recommended by the VAC on August 13, 2026, contingent upon approval of County Counsel and Risk Management; and 
3) Authorize the HHSA Director or Chief Assistant Director to execute further documents relating to these agreements, contingent upon County Counsel and Risk Management approval, as applicable, including amendments that do not increase the maximum dollar amount or term of the agreements.  

FUNDING: 100% VAC General Fund Contribution.
..Body
DISCUSSION / BACKGROUND
On March 19, 2013, the Board approved a recommendation to establish an annual allocation of Discretionary Transient Occupancy Tax (DTOT) funds, beginning with the FY 2013-14 budget, for the purpose of funding projects, programs, and services that directly benefit the support and recognition of veterans in El Dorado County (Legistar file 13-0280). On an annual basis, the Board has approved the VAC recommendations for the utilization of funding during each subsequent fiscal year. Prior to July 1, 2018, County Veteran Services (VS) had been administratively supported by the Chief Administrative Office, and funds were distributed according to the VAC directly from the General Fund. Effective July 1, 2018, VS transitioned to HHSA and DTOT funding is included in a VAC Special Revenue Fund budget. The annual allocation amount for the support and recognition of veterans was set at a fixed rate beginning with FY 2020-21 and currently receives an annual allocation of $175,000. 

The annual allocation of $175,000 is included in the FY 2026-27 County budget. The $175,000 allocation is comprised of $133,581 in FY 2026-27 General Fund contribution to the VAC and $41,419 in VAC Special Revenue Fund balance. On August 13, 2026, the VAC voted (minutes approved September 10, 2026) on the FY 2026-27 $175,000 fund distribution, and intends to allocate $78,000 to various organizations to provide support to veterans, as well as $37,197 to fund a 0.50 Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) Office Assistant position for VS, with the remaining $59,803 allocated to the El Dorado Community Foundation for $56,812.85 in mini-grants for services for veterans and $2,990.15 for a five percent administrative fee. 
 
The VAC recommendation for full utilization of the FY 2026-27 allocation is as follows:
1) Agreement 10613, Military Family Support Group - $19,000 for outreach and supportive services. 
2) Agreement 10614, El Dorado County Veterans Alliance - $10,000 for costs associated with coordinating and conducting Memorial Day and Veterans Day events at the Veterans Monument.
3) Agreement 10615, Sierra Chaplaincy - $4,000 for chaplains’ visits, officiating at military funerals, and grief counseling.
4) Agreement 10616, Snowline Hospice - $15,000 for hospice custodial care and medical equipment.
5) Agreement 10618, Lake Tahoe Community College - $8,000 for books, materials, and resources at campus Veteran Resource Centers, and improvements to the Veteran Resource Center.

..Title
HEARING - Recorder-Clerk’s Office recommending the Board conduct a public hearing to Introduce and Adopt Ordinance 5272 amending Sections 3.25 of the El Dorado County Ordinance Code to update the Recorder-Clerk’s Schedule of Fees, with fee changes to become effective January 1, 2027.
 
FUNDING:  N/A
..Body
DISCUSSION / BACKGROUND
California Government Code Chapter 12.5 County Fees, Section 54985, authorizes the Board of Supervisors to "recover the cost of providing any product or service . . " (Attachment A).  Chapter 3.25 of Title 3 of the El Dorado County Ordinance Code describes the services and products which the Recorder-Clerk provides on a fee basis. 
 
On November 5, 2019, the Board approved Ordinance 5108 amending Title 3 Revenue and Finance, Chapters 3.25 to update the schedule of fees and fee changes.  Since the adoption of the current Fee Schedule, the Recorder-Clerk's Office has seen an increase in the cost for services.
 
On September 22, 2026, the Board granted conceptual approval for the Recorder-Clerk’s Office to update the fees recovering the costs of providing services. Staff reviewed the cost of providing services based on the Fiscal Years 2024-25 budget (Attachment B - Recorder-Clerk Fee Study).  The study reflected a decrease in Recorder-Clerk’s Office fully-burdened hourly rate from $119 to $111 due to various efficiencies implemented in the Recorder-Clerk's office, changes in software, and a reduction of staff in Fiscal Year 2024-25. The cost of providing services is determined by multiplying the time required for the service by the hourly rate. Those fees that are not mandated by statute are adjusted to recover more of the County costs to provide the services. While the Recorder-Clerk’s Office fully-burdened rate has declined, many fees are increasing to reflect 100% cost recovery, when the past Fee Study sought to obtain between 49% to 84% cost recovery. 
 
Attachment C provides a red-line version of the updated fee schedule. Attachment D provides a clean version of the updated fee schedule.  
 
This Ordinance is proposed for approval and adoption pursuant to Government Code (GOV) subsection (§) 54985 and County Ordinance Code Section 1.04.260, following today's required public meeting (GOV § 54986).  The Ordinance has been noticed (Attachment E) and may be passed at today's meeting with no second reading.  If approved, the Ordinance will take effect 30 days from execution. The new fees will begin being collected January 1, 2027, with the exception of the Deed and Mortgage Notification Fee (Senate Bill 255) which will not begin collection until April 1, 2027.

The Board could choose not to approve this revised ordinance and the Recorder-Clerk would continue to offset the cost of services with Recorder Restricted Reve

..Body
DISCUSSION / BACKGROUND
The term of the current MOU between the County of El Dorado (County) and the El Dorado County Employees’ Association, Local 1, AFSCME Council 57 (Union) representing employees in the General (GE), Professional (PL), and Supervisory (SU) bargaining units, ends on December 31, 2026. 
 
Pursuant to the Meyers-Milias-Brown Act (Government Code sections 3500 et seq.), representatives of the Union and the County (collectively, the Parties) have met and conferred in good faith regarding wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment of employees in the GE, PL, and SU bargaining units. The Parties jointly prepared a successor MOU for the term of January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2026, reflecting agreed revisions to certain terms and conditions. Subject to the provisions in the MOU, a summary of the changes are listed below:

1. Effective the first full pay period containing January 1, 2027, the County will increase base wages for benchmark classifications and internally tied non-benchmark classifications to approximately eight percent (+/- 8%) of the total compensation median of the County’s February 2026 comparable agency compensation survey, with the exception of the Associate Civil Engineer, Cook II, Mental Health Clinician II, Public Health Nurse II, and Social Worker II benchmark classifications. The Associate Civil Engineer, Cook II, Mental Health Clinician II, Public Health Nurse II, and Social Worker II benchmark classifications and their internally tied non-benchmark classifications will receive an increase to approximately five percent (+/- 5%) of the total compensation median of the County’s February 2026 comparable agency compensation survey.

The classification of Hazardous-Materials/Recycling Specialist will receive a four and one-half percent (4.5%) base wage increase, consisting of an increase to (+/- 8%) of the median and an additional 2.75% (non-compounding) increase to address compaction.

2. Effective the first full pay period in January 2028, the County will increase base wages by 3.0% for all classifications subject to this MOU.

3. Modification of existing On-Call language; increase rate from $2.50/hr to $3.00/hr and limit 20% rate to specific Health and Human Services Agency classifications.

Other Terms and Conditions which are recommended for update, and which have little or unknown direct cost impact include, but are not limited to:

• Modification of existing language pertaining to sick leave for
